newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares erase losses, end up in high volume.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares erase losses, end up in high volume.

text.p: Brazil shares ended up Tuesday after trading lower early in the session, with investors again cutting positions on Telebras stocks and moving into other blue-chips and second tier issues.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active shares closed up 0.85 percent at 13,617 points. Turnover returned to recent usual daily average levels, totalling 1.101 billion reais ($1.020 billion).
Traders said the market opened lower, weighed down by a local newspaper report on warnings by investor George Soros that world stock markets could be on the verge of a crash.
O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper said Soros told German maganize Focus that "panic among unexperienced investors" could cause the crash.
The report, traders said, was also an excuse for investors to intensify the short-term profit-taking that began Monday.
The index also fell sharply earlier because of Telebras preferred, which dropped to 171.20 reais before closing at 174.20 reais, off only a slight 0.46 percent, they added.

While Telebras closed down, other blue-chips ended the day with significant gains. Federal power utility Eletrobras surged 6.6 percent at 775 reais, posting the highest rise, followed by Petrobras, which jumped 4.13 percent to 328 reais.
Private miner Vale do Rio Doce rose 5.14 percent to close at 30.70 reais on positive prospects for the company.
On Tuesday, the chairman of the recently-privatized firm Benjamin Steinbruch said the company will invest 800 million reais in 1997, up from the 600 million reais previously planned.

Analysts said the market could open firmer Thursday, when trading will resume after Wednesday's holiday in Sao Paulo, boosted by tomorrow's opening of price bids from groups seeking to win concessions to operate Band B cellular services for the Sao Paulo region.
Bids are widely expected to be much higher than the base price of 600 million reais asked by the government.
